question: If the cost of 13 kg onions is ₹273, cost of 21 kg tomatoes is ₹462 and the cost of 27 kg potatoes is ₹ 594, then find the total cost of 21 kg onions, 25 kg tomatoes and 32 kg potatoes.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Onion rate = 273 ÷ 13 = 21

Tomato rate = 462 ÷ 21 = 22

Potato rate = 594 ÷ 27 = 22

Total cost = 21×21 + 25×22 + 32×22

= 441 + 550 + 704 = 1695

**∴ Answer = 1695**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

13 kg onions = 273, 21 kg tomatoes = 462, 27 kg potatoes = 594

**Formula used:**

Unit price = Total cost ÷ Quantity

**Calculation:**

⇒ Onion price per kg = 273 ÷ 13 = 21

⇒ Tomato price per kg = 462 ÷ 21 = 22

⇒ Potato price per kg = 594 ÷ 27 = 22

⇒ Cost of 21 kg onions = 21 × 21 = 441

⇒ Cost of 25 kg tomatoes = 25 × 22 = 550

⇒ Cost of 32 kg potatoes = 32 × 22 = 704

⇒ Total cost = 441 + 550 + 704 = 1695

**∴ The correct answer is 1695.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method

Find cost per unit first, then multiply by required quantity

Direct Proportion

Cost ∝ Quantity when rate is constant

Quick Division Trick

Break numbers into factors for faster division

Efficiency Tip

Always compute unit rates first to simplify multi-item problems
